public_rationale: The October 8, 2024 compositionality report finds consistent performance gaps between familiar and unseen compositions across tested models, including GPT-4 [e1]. OpenAI's October 30 SimpleQA report documents factuality problems and reports GPT-4o scoring below 40% on deliberately challenging factual questions [e2]. The October 7 GSM-Symbolic report finds that changing numerical values reduces performance across all tested models, showing fragility in mathematical reasoning [e3]. Together, these evaluations support persistent weaknesses in all three named domains entering 2025 [e1, e2, e3]. ARC Prize's December 20 report shows substantial progress: the high-compute o3 preview scored 87.5% on its semi-private evaluation [e4]. That benchmark result does not establish reliable solutions across the three domains [e4].
limitations: The evaluations cover bounded tasks and model samples. They do not establish typical error rates across everyday use [e1, e2, e3].
The supplied compositionality excerpt describes human evaluation procedures but does not show their results [e1].
The supplied SimpleQA excerpt does not establish testing of o1-preview or whether browsing was available [e2].
GSM-Symbolic's observed performance drops do not prove its broader hypothesis that models cannot perform genuine logical reasoning [e3].
The ARC result concerns the December 2024 o3 preview and one benchmark. The supplied excerpt does not describe specific remaining failures [e4].
These items do not establish historical priority for Marcus's earlier writings or assess unnamed additional weaknesses.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Weaknesses in compositionality, factuality and reasoning persist in current AI.

statement.excerpt: The specific weak spots I raised in 2022 and going back to my 2001 book The Algebraic Mind —compositionality, factuality, reasoning, etc—persist.
statement.document_title: 25 AI Predictions for 2025, from Marcus on AI

from_speaker: current techniques have thus far not been adequate
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that significant weaknesses remained in each of the three named capabilities. It does not assert that models lack these abilities entirely or that no progress occurred.
The retrospective concerns the state of AI entering 2025. I use October through December 2024, the latest completed quarter before publication, for contemporary evaluations.

Compositionality means reliably combining familiar components or relations in unfamiliar combinations; factuality means producing accurate factual answers; reasoning means reliably carrying out valid inferences or problem-solving steps.
Support requires evidence covering all three named domains. Evidence in only one or two domains cannot establish the full claim.
The references to 2001 and 2022 identify the weaknesses under discussion. This assessment does not award historical priority or verify the contents of the earlier book.
The unspecified 'etc' supplies no additional testable domain.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporary, documented evaluations of then-current language models, including leading models, demonstrate recurring weaknesses in all three named domains: compositionality, factuality, and reasoning.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Broad, reproducible contemporary evidence establishes that at least one named domain was reliably solved across varied relevant tasks, rather than merely improved on selected benchmarks. Evidence supporting remaining weaknesses in other domains would warrant a mixed assessment.

evidence.publisher: Xiyan Fu and Anette Frank; arXiv version accepted to Findings of EMNLP 2024
evidence.explanation: The October evaluation reports systematic performance gaps between familiar and unseen graph compositions, with human evaluation confirming the direction. This supports persistence of compositionality weaknesses, while its limited task family prevents a universal conclusion.

evidence.excerpt: Current language models sometimes produce false outputs
evidence.locator: Opening paragraph, before About the SimpleQA benchmark
evidence.explanation: OpenAI documents continuing factuality problems and evaluates GPT-4o and o1-preview, among other models, on short factual questions without browsing. The dataset deliberately targets difficult questions, so its results establish remaining weaknesses rather than everyday error prevalence.

Controlled variations of mathematical problems expose recurring fragility in the tested models' reasoning performance. This supports an unresolved weakness without adopting the authors' stronger hypothesis that models cannot perform genuine logical reasoning.

The benchmark operator reports substantial progress in adaptation to unfamiliar tasks for the o3 preview. This qualifies any suggestion of stagnation, but does not establish reliable solutions across the three named domains; the same report describes remaining failures.
